mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuing state is an Apostille Convention member; otherwise consular legalization by the Canadian embassy/consulate in the issuing state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of current memorandum of association and articles of association/incorporation (or equivalent constitutional documents) of the foreign parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registry or parent company secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, as applicable to the issuing state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution approving the incorporation of the Alberta ULC, initial capital structure, and appointment of initial directors/authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized corporate minutes; Hague Apostille or consular legalization if the resolution will be relied upon by an Alberta public authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing the Alberta registered agent and local law firm for incorporation filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, as applicable to the issuing state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Chartered bank holding the parent/UBO accounts

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every UBO holding 25% or more, all directors, officers, authorized signatories, and, if applicable, the shipyard project counterparty. Screening sources include (i) Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions list (United Nations Act, Special Economic Measures Act, and Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Magnitsky)); (ii) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List and sectoral sanctions list; (iii) Politically Exposed Persons lists (foreign and domestic PEPs, heads of international organizations, and close associates/family); (iv) FINTRAC record-keeping and verification requirements under the PCMLTFA; and (v) adverse media and international debarment registers (e.g., World Bank sanctions). Any positive match triggers enhanced due diligence, compliance officer approval, and, where legally required, a suspicious transaction report to FINTRAC. Screening results and source evidence must be retained for five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta), at https://www.alberta.ca/corporate-registry; filings are submitted through authorized corporate registry service providers using the provincial corporate registry system.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be composed of English or French alphabetic characters and permitted punctuation; names in other scripts must be transliterated to Roman characters for registration. A name is required to contain a distinctive element and a descriptive element, followed by a corporate legal element. For an Alberta unlimited liability corporation, the legal element must be 'ULC', 'U.L.C.', or 'Unlimited Liability Corporation'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Trust, Loan Company, Insurance, Assurance (financial-institution terms requiring financial regulators approval)
University, College, Institute (education terms requiring ministerial approval)
Royal, Crown, Chartered, Municipal (terms implying government or royal favor requiring consent)
Lawyer, Barrister, Solicitor, Notary (legal-professional terms requiring law society approval)
Hospital, Pharmacy, Medical (healthcare terms requiring ministry approval)
Olympic (protected under applicable Olympic trademark statutes)
Police, Security, Intelligence (terms implying public-protection functions requiring regulatory approval)
Amalgamated, Cooperative, Condominium (terms that may trigger other statutes or misleading connotations)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is valid for 90 days. To extend, the applicant must obtain a new NUANS report and re-file a name reservation before expiry. If the registrar rejects a name, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the Director of Corporate Registries / Service Alberta within 30 days of rejection, including a fresh NUANS report, a reasoned legal submission addressing confusion grounds, and any written consents for sensitive tokens. Alternatively, the applicant may submit a new name reservation with a different name. If administrative reconsideration is denied, judicial review may be sought in the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Alberta Rules of Court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Hybrid arrangement accepted only where the registered office is a physical street address in Alberta staffed during normal business hours to receive service of process and maintain statutory records. A purely virtual or mailbox service is not permissible for the registered office. For a commercial shipyard, at least one operational physical facility in Alberta with dedicated management and production staff is required to demonstrate commercial substance; ancillary administrative functions may be virtual.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Registered office: less than 10% likelihood of unannounced inspection by Alberta Corporate Registry. Operational shipyard: greater than 80% likelihood of unannounced or scheduled on-site inspections during vessel construction by Alberta Occupational Health and Safety authorities, Transport Canada marine safety inspectors, and municipal fire/safety officers.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee schedule - CAD 40-75 for search/report plus reservation fee (approx. USD 55)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fixed fee for Alberta ULC incorporation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9: s 9 (incorporation by articles), Part 1.1 (unlimited liability corporation status), ss 100-102 (registered office), ss 140-141 (directors and officers); Business Corporations Regulations, Alta Reg 197/1981; and Unlimited Liability Corporation Regulation, Alta Reg 148/2006, where applicable for ULC-specific filings.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, Government of Alberta (Registry Connect online portal)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 - Articles of Incorporation (with unlimited liability corporation designation) and Form 2 - Notice of Registered Office and Directors; Certificate of Incorporation is issued by the Corporate Registry upon filing
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up or authorized capital and no escrow account or capital deposit requirements under the ABCA for a ULC; nominal authorized capital (e.g., 100 unlimited-liability common shares at CAD 0.01 par value) is lawful, but shareholders of a ULC carry joint and several unlimited liability for the corporation's obligations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the corporation accepts and adopts the Articles of Incorporation of Canadian Oceanic Shipbuilding ULC and the share subscription agreements tendered by the incorporators for a total of 100 Ordinary Unlimited Liability Shares, par value CAD 0.01, being the entire authorized and issued share capital. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the corporation shall be located at [address], Calgary, Alberta, T2P 1J9, and that the corporation shall be constituted as an unlimited liability corporation. FURTHER RESOLVED, that John A. Macdonald be appointed President and Chief Executive Officer and Jane A. Smith be appointed Corporate Secretary, and that they are authorized to execute incorporation filings, open banking arrangements, and engage professional advisors. CARRIED unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction) - NUANS name search window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS preliminary corporate name search through an authorized Alberta service provider or the Registry Connect portal; select the proposed name 'Canadian Oceanic Shipbuilding ULC'; ensure no confusingly similar trademarks or restrained words appear in the search report; pay the CAD 20 name search fee and obtain a 90-day name reservation record to be attached to the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Request for NUANS name search and reservation receipt
NUANS corporate name search report (issued within the previous 90 days)
Proposed shipyard corporate name memorandum
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for confusion or restricted wording, file a fresh NUANS search on an alternative proposed name and resubmit; a written objection response distinguishing the maritime/shipbuilding mark may be lodged with the Corporate Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators and founding directors; professional corporate law firm; Alberta Corporate Registry for form standards
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Form 1 - Articles of Incorporation for the unlimited liability corporation, inserting the reserved corporate name, registered office city (Calgary, Alberta), authorized share structure (100 ordinary unlimited-liability shares, CAD 0.01 par value), no transfer restriction unless agreed, and the express unlimited liability corporation designation; each incorporator must execute the articles in the presence of a witness and signatures should be notarized where a third-party filer is engaged.
required_dossiers: Executed Form 1 - Articles of Incorporation (ULC designation)
NUANS name search report
Written consents of nominated directors to act
Completed Form 2 - Notice of Registered Office and Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Upon a registry deficiency query, correct the article text or director consents and resubmit with a cure letter; if director consent is missing, obtain prescribed consents and attach to the response within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Instruments and Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Registry Connect online platform)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload Form 1 and Form 2 with the dossiers to Registry Connect; pay the statutory CAD 250 (approx. USD 185) electronic filing fee by credit card; the registry will stamp and return the Certificate of Incorporation together with the registered office and directors notice; the Certificate identifies the corporate number and initiates corporate existence as a ULC.
required_dossiers: Form 1 - Articles of Incorporation (signed)
Form 2 - Notice of Registered Office and Directors
Signed director consents
NUANS search report
Corporate Registry fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If rejected with a defect notice, cure the stated defect and pay the resubmission fee where applicable; for refusal on name grounds, request reconsideration in writing with a certified NUANS analysis to the Registrar of Corporations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Corporate Records and CRA Business Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Secretary; Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Certificate of Incorporation, register the ULC with the CRA for corporate income tax, goods and services tax/harmonized sales tax, payroll, and importer/exporter account as required; adopt a corporate minute book at the registered office in Calgary; issue share certificates to the subscribers, file the allotment ledger and register any unanimous shareholder agreement, and maintain the directors' register per ABCA books and records rules.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Registered office and directors notice (Form 2)
Minute book, share certificates and shareholders register
CRA RC1 business registration information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or registry notices identify missing records, cure by depositing updated corporate records in the minute book, filing any late notice to the Corporate Registry, and responding to CRA information requests with certified copies of the incorporating documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining Municipal, Industrial and Preliminary Environmental Permits for the Shipyard
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Applicable Alberta municipality (development/business licensing), Alberta Municipal Affairs - Safety Codes, Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA), and Alberta Fire Code/OHS authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a zoning-compliant development permit and municipal business licence for the shipyard; file the site plan covering fabrication sheds, covered drydock or haul-out slip, laydown yards and paint/coatings containment; determine the EPEA activity classification (Registration vs Full EIA) based on dredging/waterbody disturbance; schedule the pre-operational Alberta Fire Code inspection and OHS workplace clearance for confined spaces and crane operations.
required_dossiers: Municipal development permit application and site plan
Evidence of land ownership or leasehold interest
Preliminary EPEA registration or environmental screening document
Structural load design certificates for buildings, gantry cranes and drydock
Fire safety plan and OHS site plan with emergency response arrangements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a permit is refused or queried, resubmit revised drawings to the municipal planner, use the Subdivision and Development Appeal Board for land-use appeals, or file an appeal with the Alberta Environmental Appeals Board on EPEA conditions; re-scope the site layout to meet setbacks, discharge thresholds and fire-code requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA) - Industrial Approvals Division, in coordination with the applicable Alberta municipal development and business licensing department, Alberta Municipal Affairs (Safety Codes), Transport Canada Marine Safety and Security, and Alberta Occupational Health and Safety
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Industrial Business Licence and EPEA Industrial Operating Approval for Commercial Shipbuilding/Shipyard Manufacturing (ISIC 3011 / NAICS 336611)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas, Environmental Assessment and Industrial Approvals Branch
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Tier A - EPEA Registration and Preliminary Assessment for a land-based shipyard; a Full EIA Report and EPEA Approval become mandatory where in-water works disturb 1.0 hectare or more of aquatic habitat, involve dredging exceeding 1,200 m3, or generate risk to fish-bearing waters under the federal Fisheries Act consideration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: total suspended solids 50 mg/L or less, oil and grease 15 mg/L or less, pH 6.5-9.0 before discharge, with oil-water separation and secondary containment for drydock and marine railway areas; VOCs: compliance with Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives and at least 98% capture/destruction efficiency for coating and blasting operations; hazardous waste: lead-based paints, abrasive blasting grit and solvent waste manifested for disposal in accordance with Alberta hazardous waste rules and Transportation of Dangerous Goods for off-site movement.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Alberta Fire Code certification under the Safety Codes Act for fire suppression, extinguishing systems and marine drydock emergency access; structural load inspections under the Alberta Building Code for fabrication halls, crane foundations and vessel-support cradles; and Alberta Occupational Health and Safety clearance for confined spaces in vessel holds, overhead crane operations, hazardous materials storage (WHMIS/TDG) and emergency response planning.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); portal: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/services-business.html)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate an unlimited liability corporation (ULC) under the Alberta Business Corporations Act and file articles with the Alberta Corporate Registry. Step 2: Register the ULC with the CRA for a 9-digit Business Number (BN) and program accounts (corporate income tax, GST/HST) via Business Registration Online or Form RC1WF 'Request for a Business Number and Certain Program Accounts'. Step 3: Apply for the GST/HST account (RT program account) because the shipyard will make taxable supplies, including zero-rated exports. Step 4: Register with the CBSA and the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) for an export/import (RD) account before exporting vessels. Step 5: Ensure a Canadian resident contact or agent is appointed for CRA service, and file any required notices under the Income Tax Act (e.g., Form T106 for non-resident ownership disclosure where applicable).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: An Alberta ULC is a Canadian taxable corporation, not a pass-through entity. For U.S. federal tax purposes, the U.S. owner may file Treasury Form 8832 to classify the ULC as a disregarded entity or partnership (check-the-box election), while Canada continues to treat it as a separate taxpayer. Canada does not provide a domestic check-the-box election. The ULC may use ITA subsection 85 rollover elections on asset transfers, and must comply with Canada's hybrid mismatch disallowance rules (ITA section 18.5 and related provisions) if cross-border arrangements produce hybrid outcomes; no elective waiver of those rules is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) / Harmonized Sales Tax (HST); Alberta imposes only the federal GST at 5% with no provincial sales tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000: a person making taxable supplies in Canada (including zero-rated exports) must register for GST/HST when its total taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in any single calendar quarter or over the four preceding consecutive calendar quarters; a commercial shipyard will exceed this threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate a real-time electronic invoicing or fiscal clearance system for GST/HST, and there is no digital stamping regime. CRA requires electronic filing of GST/HST returns for most registrants (e.g., all registrants whose annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 1.5 million, and generally all corporate registrants). For exports, CBSA CERS electronic export declarations are mandatory for controlled goods and for goods valued above CAD 2,000.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A new deep-sea container vessel sold by the Alberta ULC shipyard may be zero-rated under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act if: (i) the ULC is a GST/HST registrant; (ii) the supply is a taxable supply of tangible personal property; (iii) the vessel is physically exported from Canada, generally within 60 days after delivery or within the longer period permitted under CRA's GST/HST Memorandum 7-2; and (iv) the registrant retains sufficient written evidence of export such as a CBSA/CERS export declaration, ocean bill of lading, dock receipt, delivery confirmation, and proof of payment from the non-resident buyer. Integrated shipbuilding services are zero-rated with the vessel; separately invoiced services on exported goods may also qualify under the same export evidence rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA/CERS electronic Export Declaration (B13A) containing the export transaction number
Ocean Bill of Lading, or delivery receipt and sailing confirmation showing the vessel departed Canadian territorial waters
Commercial invoice and detailed packing list for the vessel and all installed shipyard equipment
Non-resident purchaser agreement or certificate of foreign ownership evidencing the export destination and foreign owner
Bank payment evidence (SWIFT instruction, bank statement, or remittance receipt) demonstrating payment of the export consideration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada does not prescribe a fixed 180-day FX repatriation period; the 180-day benchmark is the pipeline's assumed documentary and payment cycle and should not be read as a Canadian statutory deadline. CRA may reassess within 4 years (or 7 years for misrepresentation or neglect), deny input tax credits, recharacterize zero-rated exports as taxable, and apply interest. Penalties include ETA failure-to-register and failure-to-collect penalties, false reporting penalties up to 25% of the amount erroneously claimed in egregious cases, and criminal prosecution for wilful evasion. Clawback of GST/HST plus interest and penalties applies when export documentation is incomplete or when the vessel is put to domestic or cabotage use in Canada.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), operating with the Department of Finance Canada on exchange-rate and monetary policy, the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) on prudential supervision, and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) on anti-money-laundering enforcement. The Bank of Canada Act and the Currency Act govern the Canadian dollar and impose no exchange-control licensing function.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the ULC’s incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee CAD 50; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers administrative dissolution or strike-off of the registered corporate securities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal and Alberta provincial portion)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the ULC’s fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; daily compound interest; director’s and officer’s liability for withheld amounts; possible criminal prosecution for gross negligence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Remittance Return (if annual filing elected)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due one month after the fiscal year-end for annual remitters; monthly or quarterly remittance applies to registrants with annual gross revenues above CAD 1.5 million
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 1% of amount owing plus interest; repeated failure or false statements may result in additional negligence penalties under the Excise Tax Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, an independent audit is mandatory if the ULC is a reporting issuer or if any shareholder serves a written demand for a formal audit. A private ULC may avoid appointing an auditor by passing a unanimous shareholder resolution in lieu of audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS required for Canadian public enter­prises; the private Alberta ULC may adopt Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) or voluntarily elect IFRS under CPA Canada Handbook–Accounting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta ULC must maintain an Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) Register. Individuals holding 25% or more of shares or control must be identified, and share transfers must be recorded within 15 days. No separate annual UBO filing is made to the Registrar, but the register must be available for inspection by the Registrar or law enforcement.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)
Minute Book containing resolutions, by-laws, and meeting minutes

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23.0% (15% federal Part I general rate after abatement and general rate reduction + 8% Alberta provincial corporate income tax). The ULC, when controlled by non-residents, is not a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC), so the 9%/2% small business rates do not apply.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays, free-zone exemptions, or M&P profits deduction (fully phased out to 0% after 2017). Applicable reliefs: 15% non-refundable SR&ED investment tax credit on qualifying research expenditures; CCA Class 43 (30% declining balance) for shipyard manufacturing equipment with Accelerated Investment Incentive first-year top-up for property acquired before 2028; ocean vessels in CCA Class 7 (15% declining balance); no provincial capital tax or Alberta payroll levy on the shipyard.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal) with Alberta schedule filed via CRA Corporation Internet Filing (CIF) using CRA-certified software (e.g., Profile, TaxCycle, UFile). Alberta is a deemed province under the federal-provincial Tax Collection Agreement; no separate AT1 provincial return is submitted.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (T2, T106, NR4); quarterly corporate income tax instalments under ITA s.156
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 filing deadline: six (6) months after the fiscal year-end. Final tax payment due: two (2) months after the fiscal year-end (three (3) months for qualifying CCPCs). Quarterly instalments due on the last day of each quarter of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, incorporation jurisdiction (Alberta), mailing address, and federal tax number (BN/RT program).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State 'Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation'; enter the Alberta Canadian permanent establishment (PE) address; ensure central mind and management (CMM) indicators align with Alberta board and operational offices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CRA business activity classification code for the primary industry.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter NAICS 336611 (Ship Building and Repairing) / ISIC 3011; select 'Commercial Shipbuilding – Deep-Sea Container Vessels' to trigger the correct compliance matrix.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue including ship construction contracts, dry-dock repair, and vessel conversion revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Canadian-source revenues attributable to the Alberta PE under the PE tracing rules of ITA ss.115 and 253; exclude revenues booked by a foreign head office where no PE exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Page 2 – Box 120 (Net Income Before Taxes)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: GAAP net income reconciled to tax income for the Alberta shipyard operation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjust for transfer-pricing corrections (ITA s.247), deductible intercompany procurement charges, and treaty-specific withholding adjustments; attach contemporaneous TP documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after applying non-capital loss carryforward (20-year limit), capital cost allowance, and SR&ED deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply only losses realized in the Canadian tax consolidation perimeter of the ULC; a US check-the-box disregarded election does not change Canadian taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal Part I income tax at 15% on taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim the foreign tax credit for Alberta taxes where applicable; large non-resident groups must also compute the Part IV tax on portfolio dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alberta provincial income tax at 8% on Alberta-allocated taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the Alberta allocation schedule using gross revenue and wage/salary factors; Alberta taxable income is computed from federal taxable income without separate provincial elections.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information return and disclosure of non-arm's-length transactions with non-residents (procurement of marine steel, IP licensing, management fees, vessel sale contracts).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File when aggregate non-arm's-length transaction value exceeds CAD 1,000,000 in the taxation year; for each transaction state the resident treaty partner, nature, amount, and TP method selected.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form NR4 – Box 18 (Dividends and Other Amounts)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of amounts paid or credited to non-resident shareholders, including ULC dividends.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross dividends, the 25% statutory Part XIII WHT, and any treaty-reduced rate (5% under Canada-US Treaty Article X) substantiated by a completed Form NR301 and foreign Certificate of Residence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T2 filing: 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per full month of delay (maximum 12 months); a repeat failure within three years triggers a 10% initial penalty plus 2% monthly (ITA s.162(1)-(2)). Nil-balance T2: CAD 100 per day (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500) under s.162(1.2). Late T106: CAD 100 per day (maximum CAD 2,500) plus, for gross negligence, CAD 500 per month up to 24 months (s.162(10)). Arrears interest compounds daily at the CRA prescribed rate (s.161); Alberta imposes a parallel interest-and-penalty regime collected by the CRA.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% statutory Part XIII withholding tax on dividends paid to non-residents (ITA s.212(2)).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For a US corporate beneficial owner holding at least 10% of the ULC voting shares, the Canada-US Treaty (Article X) reduces dividend WHT to 5% (otherwise 15%). Protocol: the non-resident payee must provide to the Canadian paying agent (i) Form NR301 (Declaration of Eligibility for Treaty Benefits) and (ii) a Tax Residency Certificate or equivalent (e.g., US IRS Form 6166) confirming jurisdiction of residence; documents must be in place before payment or the 25% rate applies. Excess WHT may be reclaimed by refund application under ITA s.227(6) within two years of the end of the calendar year.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties (IP, ship design, software): statutory 25% (s.212(1)(d)); Canada-US treaty rate 10% for industrial royalties (0% for certain copyright/cultural works). Interest: statutory 25% (s.212(1)(b)); Canada-US treaty rate 0% for arm's-length interest, 10% for non-arm's-length, 15% for contingent interest. Treaty relief requires the same NR301 + TRC protocol and is administered at source by the payer.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Form T106 and contemporaneous TP documentation (Local File/Master File in substance) are required where aggregate non-arm's-length transactions with non-residents exceed CAD 1,000,000 per taxation year (ITA s.233.1). Country-by-Country reporting applies to Alberta ULCs in MNE groups with consolidated global revenue exceeding CAD 850,000,000 (Reg. s.233.8).
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Commodity marine steel, ship components, vessel sales)
Profit Split (integrated design and construction intangibles)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not operate a standalone Economic Substance Regulation fee regime (unlike UAE). However, a de facto substance test operates through ITA s.245 (GAAR), the Canada-US Treaty Limitation-on-Benefits clause (Article XXIX A), and the BEPS MLI Principal Purpose Test. The ULC must demonstrate real commercial activity in Alberta (shipyard employees, physical premises, procurement and production contracts, board meetings, bank accounts, invoicing and risk management) to retain the 5% dividend WHT, treaty benefits, and arm's-length intercompany pricing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful omission of Canadian-source shipyard revenue, forged invoices, destruction of books, or materially false T2/NR4 returns (ITA s.239).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded plus full reassessment and compound interest; on indictment imprisonment of up to five years (s.239(2)); CRA public disclosure of the conviction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who direct or knowingly acquiesce in the evasion face criminal personal liability, property seizure, assets freeze, restraint orders, and travel embargoes as a bail/probation condition; disqualification from acting as a director under Alberta corporate law.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unremitted Part XIII Withholding / Source Deductions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to deduct and remit the 25% Part XIII WHT on dividends, royalties, or interest paid to non-resident shareholders, or diversion of remittances to cover shipyard cash flow.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 10% penalty plus daily prescribed interest on the unremitted amount; the Crown holds a secured charge on all ULC assets (s.227(8), s.227(10.1)); CRA may garnish receivables and shipyard bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the full unremitted WHT, interest, and penalties (s.227.1); no reimbursement from the ULC is permitted; personal bankruptcy does not discharge the liability; cross-border collection may proceed under the Canada-US treaty and Commonwealth enforcement arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intercompany purchase of steel, ship components, design royalties, or management fees priced outside the arm's-length range without contemporaneous TP documentation or T106 filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment to arm's-length amounts under s.247(2); transfer-pricing penalty of 10% of the net upward adjustment (s.247(3)); late/grossly negligent T106 penalty of CAD 500 per month (maximum CAD 12,000 over 24 months); interest on the adjusted tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving related-party invoices without TP benchmarking are personally assessed for remittances in insolvent scenarios; the 'reasonable efforts' exemption is unavailable where no contemporaneous documentation existed at the filing date.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the ULC as a letterbox vehicle solely to convert US shareholders' income into a 5% dividend-WHT rate or to exploit hybrid-disregarded (check-the-box) loss flows without shipyard business substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR avoidance transaction voided (s.245); resulting tax benefit reassessed with compound interest; denial of treaty benefits under the Limitation-on-Benefits clause and MLI PPT; potential gross-negligence penalties under s.163.2.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who certify artificial arrangements to lenders, CRA, or FINTRAC face civil restitution and personal assessment for taxes where fraudulent conveyance is found; courts may issue a non-asset dissipation order and a travel ban pending criminal tax proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting vessel-installment payments in cash or via third parties above CAD 10,000 without large-transaction and suspicious-transaction reports to FINTRAC; incomplete beneficial-ownership records for ULC shareholders holding 25% or more.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalty of up to CAD 500,000 per contravention for a corporate entity under the PCMLTFA; money laundering is an indictable offence under Criminal Code s.462.31 punishable by up to 10 years' imprisonment; concurrent CRA penalties under the excise and income tax acts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers directing concealment of beneficial owners or transaction flows incur personal criminal liability; search warrants, restraint orders, and proceeds-of-crime forfeiture may attach to personal and corporate assets; directors may face sanctions screening debarment in maritime export-credit and letter-of-credit arrangements.
